recipes.name: Pasta with Fresh Tomatoes and Corn

steps.text: In a large pot with boiling salted water cook pasta until al dente. Drain.

Meanwhile, in a large bowl whisk together the olive oil, red wine vinegar, and dried basil. Add salt and pepper to taste. Stir in the tomatoes, corn kernels, and scallions. Let sit for 5 to 10 minutes.
Toss pasta with tomato mixture. Sprinkle with grated parmesan cheese. Garnish with fresh basil, if desired.

raw_recipe.headline: Pasta with Fresh Tomatoes and Corn
raw_recipe.description: Taste a late summer harvest in a colorful pasta sauce that needs no cooking. Simply stir cooked corn, chopped tomatoes and sliced green onions into a dressing of olive oil, red wine vinegar and basil. Toss with hot pasta and sprinkle with Parmesan.

review.reviewBody: This was great! Used cherry tomatoes cut in half, 2 ears corn on the cob, cut off. Did not have red wine vinegar, used Balsamic,vidalia onions.You could use any small pasta, followed directions for rest of recipe..yum. Great with all the fresh summer produce.

I liked this dish. I made a few tweaks. I used a whole year of corn, minced a clove of garlic. Sweated half of the garlic before adding corn and 8 oz. of medium shrimp cut into 1 inch pieces which I sauteed until the shrimp was done. I placed the green onions, remaining garlic and fresh garden tomatoes (seasoned with Penzeys sandwich sprinkle) in the bowl first. Added salt and pepper to taste and stirred to combine, then I added the vinaigrette and let it sit for 5 min. before adding the hot medium size shells. Mixed, poured into a serving bowl and topped with parmesan and 2 tbsp of julienned fresh basil. Yum.

I enjoyed this dish. I added chicken and sausage. I couldn't find fresh corn so I used frozen, tasted great. I skipped the dried basil and used fresh (about 1/4 cup). I added garlic salt and red pepper flakes as other reviewers suggested, I didn't add enough because it was still slightly bland. Next time I will add fresh garlic. I also heated everything together at the end in the pan.

I used the tomatoes out of the garden and some corn off the cob. The basil was fresh, too. I did not use scallions, instead I diced up a small yellow onion. But I used real grated parmesan, not that sawdust that Kraft sells. I also used some small pasta shells left over from a minestrone recipe. It all blends together so well. Sweet, salty, fresh. a really light and yummy salad to go with my grilled baby back ribs!

Summer Veggie Spaghetti! No hard food science here- just a red wine vinaigrette with a little anchovy paste (secret ingredient!), fresh garden tomatoes, fresh Anaheim chilis, fresh butter corn, fresh garden scallions, fresh garden basil, some chopped olives and a handful of artichoke hearts all tossed with pasta of your choice! Delicious.

A lovely, light summer dish! I made this just as written, and it was three generous servings for my family of three vegetarians. I added a bit more Parmesan and fresh basil, and I tossed it all together instead of just sprinkling it on top. This will be a summer standard.
This is fantastic!!! I actually threw the tomatoes and corn in a skillet to heat them up and carmalize them a little, then I tossed in some angel hair and then topped with freshly grated parmesan!!!

This was delicious! I used balsamic vinegar and finely chopped shallots. I used corn that I steamed on the cob and then cut off and baby heirloom tomatoes. I used both the dried and fresh basil and Parmesan cheese. It was fresh and flavorful- a wonderful light summer pasta salad.

I have never tried this recipe w/ the corn but have made some derivative of it for years. I added the corn tonight and we absolutely devoured it.... so fresh, crunchy and delicious! 

My changes.... instead of dried basil, I used dried Italian seasoning and added some marinated artichokes that were in the fridge--drained the liquid...mostly water. I used only 1 tablespoon of OO. I added a heaping tablespoon of Boscoli olive salad--a staple in our household and lots of fresh basil---much more than called for in the recipe. I let this mixture sit and marinate for a couple of hours and then topped w/ shaved, sharp provolone cheese. Full disclosure: If you take anything w/ provolone cheese on top of it to a party, it's going to give off a very strong/pungent aroma! :>)

Fresh, light, and very summery. I used the ingredients, but added the specific amounts to taste. I also added a tiny bit of onion powder and a splash of lime juice and raspberry champagne vinegar for more brightness and a fruity zest. The corn was a very nice addition for textural complexity and taste. I did use thin spaghetti as my pasta choice. Great recipe that allows flexibility to make it just how you like it!

This is very flavorful and a snap to make. I used the rest of a box of orzo (approx 8-10 oz), two cobs of sweet corn (uncooked), and cherry tomatoes cut in half. The raw corn gave the dish a great texture. Adding the scallions, basil and Parmesan cheese put this over the top. My family devoured this before I could take a pic. Delicious, and I will definitely make again!
Delicious pasta salad. Very light and refreshing. I made it with Orzo and refrigerated the pasta salad.

I doubled the recipe and used Apple Cider Vinegar instead of Red Wine Vinegar. I also added small wedges of cucumber and apple. I always tweak recipes and we love spices, so I added dried Herbs de Provence, parsley and dill and granulated garlic, onion and thyme. Instead of Parmesan, I used shredded mozarella. I let it sit in the refrigerator overnight for the flavors to meld. It was great.

Very fresh pasta dish with the brightness of the red wine vinegar. I think fresh basil was the best idea. I wish the vegetables were not just sliding around the dish. Would try again with some changes.
Very refreshing for summer. The crispy corn was a nice ingrediant.

I found this recipe to be a bit tasteless. Needs more seasoning and maybe some shrimp next time. I used all fresh ingredients (tomatoes, corn and basil) from my garden. This made it a very refreshing summer entree.

Used red onion & balsamic vinegar because that was what I had.
Very good, even my hubby loved it & he is a picky eater & usually doesn’t compliment.
Definitely will make again
Yes will make again! I made it a second time and added cut up mini color peppers. Just made it for 3rd time

My husband and I loved this pasta salad - it was fresh and delicious, one of the best pasta salads I have had. I followed the recipe fairly closely. I used canned corn and used the whole can instead of 1/2 a cup. My husband likes a lot of dressing so I added 2 T of olive oil and 2 T of red wine vinegar to the amount stated in the recipe and I also added cooked shrimp since we are not vegetarians and he likes meat. Cooked, diced chicken would be another option next time. It was a wonderful salad and I will definitely make it again. Thank you so much for a great recipe.

I made this recipe as written. It was delicious! I ate 2 servings, and I don't even care for pasta that much. I think I will add a full cup of corn next time because my husband loves corn. Also I don't think the 1 tablespoon of Parmesan cheese added much to the recipe. I will leave that out next time.
